name: Backward Reachability DP
summary: Mark the last index as reachable, then scan right to left: an index is reachable if any index within its jump range is already known to reach the end.
visualizationIntent: init: the last cell is marked reachable (green); all others unknown. loop: the i cursor scans right to left; for each i the j cursor probes the cells within its jump range. check: if a probed cell is already reachable, mark i reachable (green) and stop probing. return: whether index 0 ended up reachable.

lineExplanations.4: Assume no index can reach the end yet.
lineExplanations.5: The last index trivially reaches itself — mark it reachable.
lineExplanations.6: Start scanning from the second-to-last index.
lineExplanations.7: Work right to left until index 0 is decided.
lineExplanations.8: The farthest index reachable in one jump from i (capped at the last index).
lineExplanations.9: Probe the neighbours just after i.
lineExplanations.10: Look at each index within i's jump range.
lineExplanations.11: If that neighbour already reaches the end, so can i.
lineExplanations.13: Stop probing once one good neighbour is found.
lineExplanations.14: Otherwise try the next neighbour in range.
lineExplanations.15: Move the scan one index to the left.
lineExplanations.16: The answer is whether the start index became reachable.
lineExplanations.17: Return whether the end is reachable from index 0.

syntaxExplanations.1: class Solution: defines the class wrapper expected by the platform.
syntaxExplanations.2: def canJump(self, nums): receives the jump-length array.
syntaxExplanations.4: dp = [False] * n marks every index as not-yet-reachable.
syntaxExplanations.5: dp[n - 1] = True marks the last index reachable.
syntaxExplanations.6: i = n - 2 starts one before the last index.
syntaxExplanations.7: while i >= 0: scans right to left.
syntaxExplanations.8: reach = min(i + nums[i], n - 1) is the farthest index one jump can land on.
syntaxExplanations.9: j = i + 1 begins probing at the first reachable neighbour.
syntaxExplanations.10: while j <= reach: covers every index in i's jump range.
syntaxExplanations.11: if dp[j]: is true when neighbour j already reaches the end.
syntaxExplanations.12: dp[i] = True records that i reaches the end too.
syntaxExplanations.13: break stops probing after the first good neighbour.
syntaxExplanations.14: j = j + 1 advances to the next neighbour in range.
syntaxExplanations.15: i = i - 1 moves the scan left.
syntaxExplanations.16: answer = dp[0] is whether index 0 is reachable.
syntaxExplanations.17: return answer reports whether the end can be reached.
